VBO:0201031.summary: Poitevins still work in packs on deer trails in their native Poitou, a living thread of the region's hunting tradition. French huntsmen favor them on open, relatively dry ground and choose sturdier hounds for thick, wet country; that terrain preference explains where their light-footed running style is most useful.
VBO:0201031.shortDescription: A Poitou pack hound used on deer trails, especially suited to open, drier hunting country.
VBO:0201031.historicalRoots: Poitou pack-hunting tradition, still used on deer trails.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 24: Poitevin
sources.evidence: Identifies French large scenthound and working-trial tradition; describes free, bounding movement. It does not supply breed-specific household temperament.

sources.title: Société de Vènerie: Le type de chien
sources.evidence: French hunting association says Poitevins are especially suited to open, relatively dry country; heavier Anglo-French and Foxhounds are favored in thickets and wet ground.

sources.title: Société de Vènerie: Equipage du Haut Poitou profile
sources.evidence: Association describes the Haut Poitou kennel in the Moulière forest, its more than century-long deer-hunting tradition, and its Poitevin and French Tricolore pack.

VBO:0201418.summary: Westphalian Dachsbrackes are friendly, adaptable hunters with a fine nose and a strong passion for following a track. Pure breeding of these smaller, low-running hounds began in the 1880s as hunting grounds shrank; they kept the working role of the German Bracke in a sturdier, short-legged frame.
VBO:0201418.shortDescription: A friendly, track-focused small hound developed for the tighter hunting grounds of Westphalia.
VBO:0201418.historicalRoots: Westphalian small running hound developed in the 1880s for smaller hunting grounds.

sources.title: VDH: Westfälische Dachsbracke breed profile
sources.evidence: States adaptable, friendly hunting dog with fine nose and strong tracking passion; says pure breeding of small running hounds began in the 1880s as hunting grounds became smaller.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 100: Westphalian Dachsbracke
sources.evidence: Identifies the short-legged variety of German Bracke, 30–38 cm sturdy small hound, with working-trial use, red/yellow with black mantle and white markings, sabre or gently curved tail.

VBO:0201163.summary: Saint Germain Pointers tend to be sociable, even-tempered and affectionate, yet their hunting focus is clear: they range for pheasant, partridge and woodcock and retrieve with a soft mouth. Developed around 1830 in French royal kennels, the breed became an early dog-show favorite while remaining a working bird dog.
VBO:0201163.shortDescription: A sociable French pointer that hunts birds with focus and retrieves them with a soft mouth.
VBO:0201163.historicalRoots: French royal kennels at Compiègne and Saint-Germain-en-Laye, around 1830.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 115: Braque Saint-Germain
sources.evidence: Temperament: sociable, equable, affectionate; hunting pheasant, partridge and woodcock with soft-mouth retrieval; development around 1830 at royal kennels in Compiègne and Saint-Germain-en-Laye; early dog-show history.

VBO:0200634.summary: Greek Sheepdogs are independent, watchful flock guardians that often patrol the edge of a herd to survey the wider ground. Their work calls for a protective response to intruders and steady movement over difficult mountain terrain, while they remain settled among the animals they guard.
VBO:0200634.shortDescription: An independent Greek flock guardian that patrols the herd’s edge and watches for intruders.

sources.title: Greek Sheepdog Club (OFEP): breed standard
sources.evidence: Greek-language club standard describes independent, courageous, vigilant protective character; patrolling the flock perimeter, reacting to intruders, steady rough-terrain movement, and calm coexistence with the flock. Do not claim unverified ancient lineage.

VBO:0200015.summary: Alaskan Huskies are selected for a strong desire to run and the speed and endurance needed in sled work. Rather than a fixed pedigree look, this working type has been bred by mushers for practical northern traits; individuals can vary considerably in build and coat even while sharing the demands of the trail.
VBO:0200015.shortDescription: Selected for the drive to run, speed and endurance, this variable working type is shaped by sled teams.
VBO:0200015.historicalRoots: Alaskan working sled-dog breeding focused on racing function rather than show appearance.

sources.title: Iditarod: Sled Dog Genetics
sources.evidence: Describes Alaskan Husky as a selectively bred sled-dog type for speed, northern traits and working ability, with varying appearance and no fixed pedigree standard.

sources.title: Iditarod: What Makes a Good Sled Dog? Part 1
sources.evidence: Describes Alaskan huskies as composite dogs bred for racing at short and long distances, speed and endurance, and says sled dogs’ drive to run is cultivated through training. Do not assign every individual the same temperament.

VBO:0200952.summary: Northern Inuit Dogs tend to be friendly, placid and outgoing, with an inquisitive streak that rewards varied training. Developed in Britain from northern breeds and German Shepherds beginning in the 1980s, they were shaped for a wolf-like outline while remaining domestic companions.
VBO:0200952.shortDescription: A friendly, inquisitive British-developed dog with a northern outline and a need for varied training.
VBO:0200952.historicalRoots: British Northern Inuit breeding program begun in the 1980s.

sources.title: American Northern Inuit Society: Our Breed
sources.evidence: Society history traces the British breeding program to the early 1980s and describes its own standard temperament as friendly, placid and outgoing; training section says intelligent dogs may become bored and benefit from varied work. Claims scoped to the Society account; do not assert wolf ancestry or universal behavior.

VBO:0201049.summary: Medium Poodles are lively, joyful companions prized for loyalty and their ability to learn. Poodles began as waterfowling dogs before becoming companions across four sizes; the medium variety carries that shared working history and trainable character in a compact, athletic frame.
VBO:0201049.shortDescription: An alert, trainable medium Poodle whose history runs from waterfowling to companionship.
VBO:0201049.historicalRoots: French Poodle tradition with older waterfowling use and companion breeding.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 172: Poodle
sources.evidence: FCI identifies original waterfowling use, friendly/joyful/loyal character, trainability, black as a solid coat color and Medium height over 35 to 45 cm. No coat-color-specific behavioral claim.

VBO:0201152.summary: Longhaired Russian Toys are active, cheerful and curious companions, with a close bond to their people described in the FCI standard. The fringed variety arose in Moscow after a 1958 litter produced a pup with striking ear and leg feathering; that coat became part of a distinct Russian line rather than an English Toy Terrier variant.
VBO:0201152.shortDescription: A cheerful, curious little companion whose fringed-ear variety emerged in Moscow in 1958.
VBO:0201152.historicalRoots: Russian Toy revival in the mid-1950s; longhaired variety first noted in a 1958 Moscow litter.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 352: Russian Toy
sources.evidence: FCI calls Russian Toy active, cheerful, curious and devoted; records the 1958 Moscow birth of the longhaired form and its fringed ears and limbs. It is a companion breed.

VBO:0201187.summary: Schnauzers balance a lively, playful character with composure and alert watchfulness. The breed began as a southern German stable dog that kept rodents down around horses, then became a watch and companion dog. Its keen senses and trainability continue that practical working tradition.
VBO:0201187.shortDescription: A lively yet composed German stable ratter and watchdog in a wiry pepper-and-salt coat.
VBO:0201187.historicalRoots: Southern German stable ratter, later watch and companion dog.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 182: Schnauzer
sources.evidence: FCI describes lively but composed, playful and alert breed character, stable and rodent-catching history in southern Germany, and pepper-and-salt color. No color-specific personality; no guarantee of individual suitability.

VBO:0200849.summary: Majorca Shepherd Dogs are intelligent and affectionate toward their person while often reserved with strangers. They were bred on the Balearic Islands for shepherding, guarding and defense, work that calls for a close response to a familiar handler and watchfulness around newcomers. The shorthaired form is the more common of two varieties.
VBO:0200849.shortDescription: An intelligent, watchful Balearic shepherd and guard dog; this is its common shorthaired form.
VBO:0200849.historicalRoots: Balearic island shepherding and guarding tradition.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 321: Chien de Berger de Majorque
sources.evidence: French FCI standard identifies Balearic origin, shepherd/guard use, shorthaired variety as more widespread, and intelligent/affectionate with its person/reserved with strangers breed character. Short coat, black color and tail to hock are morphological controls.

VBO:0200217.summary: Bracco Italianos are reliable, docile pointing dogs with the toughness to work through varied kinds of hunting. Italian bird hunters have used this breed for centuries, and its ready response to a handler sits alongside a strong field purpose.
VBO:0200217.shortDescription: A docile, reliable Italian bird pointer with centuries of varied field work behind it.
VBO:0200217.historicalRoots: Italian bird-hunting and pointing tradition documented from the fourteenth century.

sources.title: FCI standard 202
sources.evidence: FCI 202 utilization identifies a pointing dog; historical summary traces Italian sporting use; temperament section documents adaptation to hunting and a docile, reliable character.

VBO:0200511.summary: Estrela Mountain Dogs are watchful, protective partners to shepherds, traditionally guarding flocks against predators and thieves. The standard also describes them as devoted to familiar people and wary of strangers. Their work spans the slopes and high pastures of Portugal’s Estrela Mountains.
VBO:0200511.shortDescription: A watchful Portuguese flock guardian, devoted to familiar people and wary of strangers.
VBO:0200511.historicalRoots: Flock guarding in Portugal’s Estrela Mountains, from foothills to summer high pasture.

sources.title: FCI standard 173
sources.evidence: FCI 173 describes traditional Portuguese livestock guardianship, alertness and a protective disposition; these are breed-wide tendencies and not coat personalities.

VBO:0200605.summary: Giant Schnauzers are even-tempered, good-natured workers with a history that began in southern German cattle driving. Breeders later valued their endurance and steadiness in utility work, a shift from moving livestock to jobs that demanded a durable, responsive partner.
VBO:0200605.shortDescription: An even-tempered southern German working dog, first used to drive cattle across the region.
VBO:0200605.historicalRoots: Southern German cattle driving, followed by broader utility work.

sources.title: FCI standard 181
sources.evidence: FCI 181 historical summary records cattle driving and later utility; temperament section documents an even, good-natured and reliable working character.

VBO:0200625.summary: Great Danes tend to be devoted to their people and self-possessed around new encounters; the standard calls for a confident, tractable companion without aggression. Their modern German identity brought several older large-dog types under one breed name in the late nineteenth century.
VBO:0200625.shortDescription: A devoted, confident German companion with a calm manner and an imposing history.
VBO:0200625.historicalRoots: German consolidation of several large-dog types under the Great Dane name in 1878.

sources.title: FCI standard 235
sources.evidence: FCI 235 records companion/watch history and describes a friendly, devoted, confident character with nonaggressive temperament.

VBO:0200626.summary: Great Danes are expected to be friendly and devoted to familiar people, confident rather than combative when they meet the wider world. Today the breed is a companion and watch dog, though its German history reaches back through older hunting and mastiff-type dogs.
VBO:0200626.shortDescription: A friendly, devoted Great Dane whose confident presence reflects its companion and watch role.
VBO:0200626.historicalRoots: German companion and watch breed developed from older hunting and mastiff-type dogs.

sources.title: FCI standard 235
sources.evidence: FCI 235 records German Great Dane history and describes friendly, devoted and confident character; no fawn-specific temperament is asserted.

VBO:0200676.summary: Hovawarts are even-tempered, protective working dogs with a notably good nose. Their German name recalls a guardian of the farm or yard, while the modern standard also places them in tracking and rescue work that draws on their scenting ability.
VBO:0200676.shortDescription: An even-tempered German guardian with a good nose and a modern tracking and rescue role.
VBO:0200676.historicalRoots: German yard-guardian tradition; modern tracking and rescue work.

sources.title: FCI standard 190
sources.evidence: FCI 190 historical and temperament sections document yard-guardian name, protective and even disposition, scent ability, and tracking/rescue work.

VBO:0200887.summary: Miniature Bull Terriers are spirited, fun-loving companions whose resolve can show as stubbornness. The miniature line was removed from Britain’s breed register in 1918, then enthusiasts revived it with a dedicated club in 1938. The standard still asks for an even temperament and a response to discipline.
VBO:0200887.shortDescription: A spirited, fun-loving small terrier whose determined nature can sometimes become obstinate.
VBO:0200887.historicalRoots: Nineteenth-century British miniature Bull Terrier line revived in 1938.

sources.title: FCI standard 359
sources.evidence: FCI 359 historical summary covers the miniature line’s nineteenth-century presence and 1938 revival; temperament section documents spirited, fun-loving and sometimes obstinate character.

VBO:0008029.summary: Podencos Andaluces are keen, persistent field hunters with a strong instinct to pursue quarry through Andalusian cover. They use scent in the search and can work in rabbit country as well as on larger game, a range of field tasks recorded in the Spanish breed standard.
VBO:0008029.shortDescription: A keen Andalusian hunting dog used from dense rabbit cover to varied larger-game work.
VBO:0008029.historicalRoots: Andalusian hunting across rabbit cover and larger-game country.

sources.title: Real Sociedad Canina de España, Podenco Andaluz breed standard
sources.evidence: RSCE describes strong hunting instinct, scenting and work from rabbit cover to larger game; the standard separates size/hair varieties without coat-specific behavior.

VBO:0008049.summary: The Small Međimurje Dog is an alert farmyard guardian and persistent rodent catcher from northern Croatia. Its watchfulness has a voice: the breed standard describes a dog that announces unfamiliar arrivals with barking. Mills beside the Mura and Drava rivers once valued this practical small worker.
VBO:0008049.shortDescription: An alert Croatian farm dog that announces visitors and works persistently at rodent control.
VBO:0008049.historicalRoots: Farmyards and mills in Croatia’s Međimurje region near the Mura and Drava rivers.

sources.title: Suomen Medimurjenkoirat ry, Small Međimurje Dog English breed standard
sources.evidence: The breed club standard records farmyard guarding and rodent catching near the Mura and Drava rivers; temperament is persistent in work and alert toward strangers, not aggressive as a breed ideal.

VBO:0200988.summary: Pastore della Lessinia e del Lagorai dogs are attentive, balanced herders that move livestock across long, uneven alpine routes. The Italian standard describes an especially strong sense of spatial orientation and a close working bond with people. Transhumant flocks shaped this breed in the mountains and foothills of northeastern Italy.
VBO:0200988.shortDescription: An attentive alpine herder with endurance and a strong sense of direction on long drives.
VBO:0200988.historicalRoots: Northeastern Italian mountain and prealpine transhumant livestock driving.

sources.title: Ente Nazionale della Cinofilia Italiana, Cane da Pastore della Lessinia e del Lagorai standard 907
sources.evidence: ENCI 907 documents livestock driving across varied alpine terrain, alertness, spatial orientation, endurance and a balanced, human-friendly disposition. It does not assign personality by coat colour.

VBO:0200264.summary: Hotosho are balanced, confident guardians with an inborn watchfulness and strong attachment to their people. The Russian Kynological Federation describes this Buryat working dog as active and readily trained for different tasks. Its long regional history grew through folk selection rather than a single modern breeding program.
VBO:0200264.shortDescription: A confident Buryat guardian, devoted to its people and ready to learn different kinds of work.
VBO:0200264.historicalRoots: Folk-selected working guardian from Buryatia; formerly called Buryat-Mongolian dog.

sources.title: Russian Kynological Federation: Hotosho standard
sources.evidence: RKF identifies Hotosho as the former Buryat-Mongolian dog, selected in Buryatia; describes a balanced, confident, active guardian with devotion to its people and trainability across work courses.

VBO:0200378.summary: Colombian Fino Hounds can be stubborn and single-minded on a hunt, yet their breed club also describes them as friendly toward strangers and comfortable working among other dogs. Developed in Colombia from imported hounds and pointing dogs, this tracking breed became a practical companion to rural hunters as well as sporting packs.
VBO:0200378.shortDescription: A determined Colombian tracking hound, known for working in packs and greeting strangers amiably.
VBO:0200378.historicalRoots: Colombian hunting hound developed from imported European and North American hounds and pointing dogs.

sources.title: Asociación Club del Sabueso Fino Colombiano: official standard (2018)
sources.evidence: Official Colombian club standard describes a determined, stubborn hunter used for tracking, hunting and companionship; says the hound can work in groups and is friendly toward strangers. It traces its Colombian development from imported hounds and pointing dogs.

VBO:0201410.summary: Welsh Sheepdogs use their own initiative to move livestock across open hill country, while also taking direction from a handler. Their herding and guarding instincts reach back to drovers’ dogs that kept cattle and sheep together on long routes. The Welsh Sheepdog Society has worked since 1997 to preserve this native working strain.
VBO:0201410.shortDescription: An independent Welsh hill-country herder that also takes direction and watches over livestock.
VBO:0201410.historicalRoots: Welsh farm and droving dogs; preservation through the Welsh Sheepdog Society since 1997.

sources.title: Welsh Sheepdog Society: breed history and working traits
sources.evidence: The Society describes independent initiative alongside handler direction in hill-country livestock work, strong guarding and herding instincts, droving history and its 1997 preservation effort.

VBO:0201162.summary: Shorthaired Saint Bernards share the breed’s friendly, watchful nature, with a temperament the FCI describes as calm to lively. Their ancestors guarded the Great St Bernard hospice before becoming known for finding travelers lost in snow and fog. The close, dense Stockhaar coat is one form of the same mountain working breed.
VBO:0201162.shortDescription: A friendly, watchful Saint Bernard of the shorthaired variety, rooted in Alpine hospice work.
VBO:0201162.historicalRoots: Hospice dogs of the Great St Bernard Pass, historically used for guarding and traveler rescue.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 61: Saint Bernard
sources.evidence: FCI describes the breed as friendly and watchful with calm-to-lively temperament; records hospice guarding and historical search/rescue of travelers lost in snow and fog. It recognizes Stockhaar, the shorthaired variety, with no separate temperament.

VBO:0201438.summary: Miniature Xoloitzcuintles are generally quiet and calm, yet cheerful and alert; they may be reserved with strangers. The FCI classifies the miniature size as a companion, while the larger sizes have a watchdog role. This small hairless form belongs to a Mexican breed whose history reaches back to pre-Hispanic times.
VBO:0201438.shortDescription: A quiet, alert miniature Mexican companion from the Xoloitzcuintle’s ancient lineage.
VBO:0201438.historicalRoots: Pre-Hispanic Mexican Xoloitzcuintle lineage; FCI miniature companion variety.

sources.title: FCI Standard No. 234: Xoloitzcuintle
sources.evidence: FCI recognizes Miniature (25–35 cm) as companion size, describes the breed as silent/calm/cheerful, alert and potentially suspicious of strangers, and records ancient pre-Hispanic Mexican history. Hairless and coated forms are both recognized.
